title: How to Connect Slack to Notion (3 Ways)
description: Native integration, no-code automation, and API options for syncing Slack and Notion, with the tradeoffs of each.
bodyHtml:
Slack and Notion solve different problems: Slack is where conversations happen, Notion is where the resulting decisions and docs live. Connecting them means updates in a Notion page or database can trigger a Slack message, and Notion links pasted into Slack unfurl into readable previews.

MethodSetup effortBest for
Native Notion-Slack integrationLow (a few clicks)Page update notifications, unfurling Notion links in Slack
Zapier / MakeMediumCustom triggers, e.g. new database row → Slack message
API + webhook (custom)HighTwo-way sync, bulk operations, custom logic

Method 1: Notion's built-in Slack integration

Notion has an official Slack app, installable from the Slack App Directory or Notion's integration settings. Once connected, pasting a Notion page link in Slack unfurls a live preview, and you can subscribe specific pages to post edit/comment updates into a chosen channel.

Method 2: Zapier or Make (no-code automation)

For anything beyond notifications, like turning a new row in a Notion database into a formatted Slack message, use Zapier or Make:

  • Trigger: "New Database Item" in Notion
  • Action: "Send Channel Message" in Slack
  • Map Notion properties (title, status, assignee) into the Slack message text

Both platforms have free tiers that cover low-volume use (a few hundred tasks/month).

Method 3: Direct API integration (for developers)

For full control, bidirectional sync, custom formatting, rate-limit-aware batching, call both APIs directly. Notion's API works with database queries and page objects; Slack's Web API (chat.postMessage) or an Incoming Webhook handles the message side:

POST https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX
Content-Type: application/json

{ "text": "New Notion page: Q3 Roadmap" }

This is the right approach when you need logic Zapier can't express, like deduplicating updates or writing Slack thread replies back into a Notion page as comments.

Which to pick

Start with the native integration if you only need visibility. Reach for Zapier or Make once you want conditional logic without writing code. Build a custom integration only once the automation is core to your workflow and outgrows a no-code tool's rate limits.
